Georg is the founder of Pension Refund Germany. They help people get a pension payments refund after leaving Germany. When you work in Germany, 9.3% of your income goes into your public pension. If you leave Germany, you can get those pension payments back. You can get thousands of euros back. This guide explains when you can get a pension refund, and how to apply for it.

Calculate how much money you get back from a German pension payments refund. This tool requires JavaScript to work. It depends on your nationality, and the country you live in. The rules are different for every country. Use the pension refund calculator to see if you can get a refund. You can get a refund if… You are not forced to contribute to the German pension system and you can’t make voluntary German public pension contributions and your last German pension payment was more than 24 months ago and you do not make pension contributions in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia or Türkiye and you are an Indian citizen or you do not live in India To see the exact requirements, find your nationality below, or just use the pension refund calculator.

title: EU, EEA and Switzerland citizens
text: If you are a citizen of the European Union, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland, you can always contribute to your German pension, so you can’t get a refund. [toytowngermany.com, toytowngermany.com, rentenfuchs.info, Regulation (EEC) No 1408/71, § 10 para. 2] There is an exception. You can get a refund if: you are at least 67 years old and you don’t qualify for a German pension

title: Contracting countries
text: If you are a citizen of these countries, you can sometimes get a German pension refund: Albania Australia Brazil Canada Chile India Israel Japan Moldova Montenegro Morocco the Philippines South Korea Tunisia Türkiye the United States Uruguay If you can’t get a refund now, you can get a refund when you are 67 years old. You can get a pension refund if: you made less than 60 monthly pension payments in Germany and your last pension payment was more than 24 months ago and you do not live in the European Union or the United Kingdom and you are an Indian citizen or you do not live in India and you do not make pension contributions in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia or Türkiye You can also get a pension refund if: you made less than 60 monthly German pension payments and you are at least 67 years old and you live anywhere in the world

title: Citizens of other countries
text: You can get a pension refund if: your last pension payment was more than 24 months ago and you do not live in the European Union, the United Kingdom or India and you do not make pension contributions in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia or Türkiye Unlike citizens of contracting countries, you can get a refund even if you contributed to the German pension for more than 60 months. You can also get a pension refund if: you made less than 60 monthly German pension payments and you are at least 67 years old and you live anywhere in the world

section: How much money will I get back?
text: You will get a refund for all your pension payments. [§ 210 SGB VI] That’s around 9.3% of your gross income. That means you usually get a few thousand euros back. Use this refund calculator to get an exact answer. Calculate how much money you get back from a German pension payments refund. This tool requires JavaScript to work. You will not get a refund for… Your employer’s contributions to your pension The months you received Elterngeld or ALG I Contributions you have made in East Germany before June 30 1990 If you already received benefits from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung, your refund will be smaller. If you were self-employed, you probably did not make pension payments, so you get no money back. If you made voluntary pension payments, you only get 50% of your payments back (9.3% of your income). To know the exact amount of your pension refund: Request a Versicherungsverlauf from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung. It will arrive by post in 1 to 3 weeks. If you have an eID, you can get a Versicherungsverlauf instantly. or ask Pension Refund Germany, FundsBack or Germany Pension Refund to check for you. It’s free.

section: How to get your pension payments back
text: The pension refund is not automatic. You must apply for it. You can do it yourself, or pay someone to do it for you.

section: How to get your pension payments back
title: Do it yourself
text: If you apply yourself, it costs nothing. You need to fill a few different forms, and send them to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung. They will write back to you, and ask for more documents. After a few months, you will get a refund. This can be really easy, or really hard. The refunds are managed by different employees in different offices, and there is a lot of confusion. The forms are simple, but each employee asks for different things. If there is a problem, they just wait until you contact them again. For example, if a letter is lost in the mail (they don’t use registered mail), nothing happens until you contact them again. The Deutsche Rentenversicherung contacts you by post, in German. This can add long delays. If you want to do it yourself, here are the steps: Wait 24 months after your last pension payment After your last mandatory pension payment, you must wait 24 months to apply for a refund. Your last payment usually is one month after your last day of work. For example, if your last day of work was on March 5, 2018, your last payment was in April 2018. You can apply for a refund in May 2020. While you wait, you can still prepare the documents. It’s easier if you prepare the documents while you are in Germany. Find your tax ID and your social insurance number You need those numbers to fill the forms. Use this guide to find your tax ID, and this guide to find your social insurance number. Download the form package, and fill the correct form If you need help to fill the forms, you can call the Deutsche Rentenversicherung or book an appointment. If you are Turkish, you must fill form E5816. This form is in Turkish and German. Follow the German instructions in document E5817. If you are not Turkish, you must fill the standard form. Follow the German instructions in document V0910. Form V0900 in German, or form V0901 in English, French, Italian or Spanish If you are Turkish, you must fill form E5816. This form is in Turkish and German. Follow the German instructions in document E5817. If you are not Turkish, you must fill the standard form. Follow the German instructions in document V0910. Form V0900 in German, or form V0901 in English, French, Italian or Spanish Form V0900 in German, or form V0901 in English, French, Italian or Spanish Download and fill the payment information form ( Zahlungserklärung) If you use a bank in another country, your refund will take 2 months longer. The payment information form asks for a PANR, a BXNR and a ZANR. You don’t have those numbers. Leave those fields empty. If the bank account is in Germany, fill form A1310. Transfers to German bank accounts are much faster. If the bank account is in Canada or the United States, fill form A1312. If the bank account is in Italy, fill form A1311. If the bank account is in any other country, fill form A1310. If the bank account is in Germany, fill form A1310. Transfers to German bank accounts are much faster. If the bank account is in Canada or the United States, fill form A1312. If the bank account is in Italy, fill form A1311. If the bank account is in any other country, fill form A1310. Collect the other documents A certified copy of your passport The German embassy or consulate can make a certified copy of your passport. The information in your passport must be the same as in the application forms. A copy of your Meldebescheinigung zur Sozialversicherung You can use an older one. It doesn’t have to be the latest one. Deregistration certificate ( Abmeldebescheinigung) This proves that you do not live in Germany anymore. They do not always ask for this document. Proof that you live in your current country This can be a certificate from the tax office, a registration certificate, or anything that proves that you live in that country. In some cases, you must go to a German embassy to verify your identity. The Deutsche Rentenversicherung will tell you what they need after you apply. It’s different for everyone. Power of attorney ( Vollmacht) If you apply for someone else, or someone else applies for you, include a Vollmacht. A certified copy of your passport The German embassy or consulate can make a certified copy of your passport. The information in your passport must be the same as in the application forms. A copy of your Meldebescheinigung zur Sozialversicherung You can use an older one. It doesn’t have to be the latest one. Deregistration certificate ( Abmeldebescheinigung) This proves that you do not live in Germany anymore. They do not always ask for this document. Proof that you live in your current country This can be a certificate from the tax office, a registration certificate, or anything that proves that you live in that country. In some cases, you must go to a German embassy to verify your identity. The Deutsche Rentenversicherung will tell you what they need after you apply. It’s different for everyone. Power of attorney ( Vollmacht) If you apply for someone else, or someone else applies for you, include a Vollmacht. Send everything to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung Send all the required forms and documents to Deutsche Rentenversicherung Bund, 10704 Berlin. Don’t send your documents before the end of the 2 year waiting period. If you send your documents too early, they will send them back to you. Wait for a response The Deutsche Rentenversicherung will review your case. If they need more documents, they will contact you. They will contact you by post, in German. You might need to mail more documents later. You might need to go to the German embassy or consulate to prove that you live in that country. Each employee wants something different. You must be patient. Get your refund The Deutsche Rentenversicherung will send you a letter to confirm that you want your refund. After you confirm, you might wait another 6 weeks before you get your refund.

section: How to get your pension payments back
title: Get help from someone
text: You can let someone take care of everything. There are good reasons to get help: You don’t need to speak German You can write to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung in English, but they will answer in German. They will often request more documents, and more information. If you don’t speak German, it can be confusing. You don’t need a fixed address The Deutsche Rentenversicherung will contact you by post. If you don’t have a fixed address, or if the post is not reliable, this can be a problem. Your case is processed faster The Deutsche Rentenversicherung communicates by post. If you live far from Germany, this can delay your refund by a few weeks. They do not use registered mail, so if a letter gets lost, you will wait much longer. You get your money faster If you want to receive your refund in a non-German bank account, you must wait an extra 2 months. Germany Pension Refund and FundsBack can receive the money in a German bank account, and transfer it directly to you. This saves you two months of waiting. They also offer more payment options than the Deutsche Rentenversicherung. You pay lower transaction fees These companies offer more payment options than the Deutsche Rentenversicherung. They can use services like Wise to pay you in another currency with lower conversion fees. These businesses can help you request a refund. They will fill the forms and request the refund for you. They can also check how much money you will get back. Pension Refund Germany Their fee is 10% of your refund (maximum fee € 2,800). Germany Pension Refund Their fee is 9.75% of your refund (maximum fee € 2,500). FundsBack Their fee is 9.405% of your refund (minimum fee € 854.05, maximum € 2,754.05). The Deutsche Rentenversicherung can also help you fill the forms. Their email is meinefrage@drv-bund.de. They only answer in German. You can also book an appointment and visit them in person. Germany Mantra and Pension Redemption also handle pension refunds, but their fee is higher.

You can request a pension payments refund 24 months after your last pension payment. Your last payment is usually the month after you stop working. After you apply for a refund, it takes 1 to 6 months to get your money back. It’s a long process, and it’s sometimes complicated. You can start preparing a few months before you are eligible.
The Deutsche Rentenversicherung will transfer the money to your bank account. They can send the money to any bank account, in Germany or elsewhere. Transfers to German bank accounts are much faster.

If you need help, ask… The Deutsche Rentenversicherung Call them, email meinefrage@drv-bund.de, or book an appointment. I have called them many times and they always helped, but they only speak German. Pension refund services Pension Refund Germany, FundsBack and Germany Pension Refund can request a refund for you. They speak English. They take care of everything, but they keep around 10% of your refund. Ask an expert about German pension payments refunds This tool requires JavaScript to work. Tax advisors rarely have experience with German pension refunds. German embassies and consulates do not help you with German pension refunds.
